proposedValue: Koi are pond fish: one koi needs roughly 1,000 L to start, and a group needs a pond of several thousand litres with strong filtration (filter turning the volume over at least twice an hour). proposedValue: This is not a home-aquarium fish. A juvenile can start in about 680 L (180 gal) up to roughly 75 cm, but adults need an indoor pond or stock tank of at least 305 x 152 x 91 cm (~4,164 L), with published alternatives up to 400 cm / 8,000 L. Cycle for 6-10 weeks before purchase, target 4-6x hourly turnover, and keep nitrate below 30 ppm.

proposedValue: The alligator gar is an apex ambush predator: motionless near the surface like a floating log until prey is within reach, then a burst fast enough to cause collisions in short tanks. It is not community-safe by diet rather than by aggression - anything mouth-sized is eaten, so tankmate safety is a gape measurement taken every six months, not a species list. Provide floating cover over open water so the fish feels secure at the surface, and expect a jumper that will test any lid.

proposedValue: Obligate piscivore: whole prey items only - rotating tilapia, silversides/smelt, shell-on shrimp, squid and earthworms, with a weekly vitamin B1 supplement. Never feed mammal meat (beef heart, chicken) and never build the diet on feeder goldfish or rosy reds: thiaminase destroys vitamin B1 and the damage is cumulative and irreversible, plus feeders carry parasites and disease. Feed juveniles daily, sub-adults every other day, and adults two to three times a week (SeriouslyFish says one to two meals at most); remove leftovers and keep body condition lean - fatty liver is the common overfeeding error. Transition wild-caught fish onto frozen foods with the stick-and-jiggle method rather than live feeders.

proposedValue: Default: keep it alone (SeriouslyFish). In genuinely massive systems, tankmates must pass two tests - physically impossible to swallow, and able to tolerate the same enormous enclosure. The named candidates are large arowana, freshwater stingrays, assertive large cichlids and redtail catfish in 3,000-plus gallon setups. proposedValue: Verdict: expert-only, build-first commitment. Budget a custom indoor pond or vat of at least 305 x 152 cm and 4,000+ litres (published figures run to 8,000 L), pond-grade filtration with 4-6x turnover, weekly 30-50% water changes, a six-to-ten-week fishless cycle started before you buy anything, and a cover that stops jumps without blocking air. Have a written rehoming plan (two backup homes and a tank-buster fund) and check your state's possession laws before purchase: public aquariums are full and dumping a non-native gar is both illegal and ecologically catastrophic. Skip it and keep a Florida gar if you cannot commit to all of that.

proposedValue: Gymnomuraena zebra is the sole member of its genus, a heavy-bodied, boldly banded moray with blunt molar-like teeth built for crushing shells. It is one of the widest-ranging morays on earth: FishBase records it across the Indo-West Pacific from the Red Sea and East Africa to the Society Islands, north to the Ryukyu and Hawaiian islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef, plus the eastern Pacific from southern Baja California to Colombia and the Galapagos, on reef-associated rocky and sandy bottoms from 3 to 50 m depth. proposedValue: Longnose gars are sedentary ambush predators: they hang motionless near vegetation or float at the surface - where gulping air looks like basking - then explode forward in a sudden attack on passing fish.
